CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is currently on 1 mg prednisone daily, which she reports is adequate for symptom control. She occasionally takes an additional dose approximately once weekly due to increased pain in her feet, particularly on days when she is more active. She works a desk job. Patient previously held methotrexate during COVID vaccination because she received information that it could interfere with vaccine efficacy. She experienced significant pain during that week of discontinuation and resumed methotrexate afterward. She took methotrexate with her second COVID vaccine dose based on guidance from a hotline. Patient reports methotrexate has been helpful for her joint pain. Since the methotrexate dose was increased, her knee pain has improved. Patient reports recent bruising that appears without her feeling the trauma when it occurs.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for joint pain and bruising.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (plan to discontinue)
Methotrexate (recently increased)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient examined with shoes and socks removed. Pain elicited in foot joints and other joints. Knee flexion performed; patient reports improvement compared to prior. Toe flexion demonstrates good range of motion. Nail ridges noted.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis: Patient is progressing well with current treatment regimen. Discontinue prednisone today. Continue methotrexate, which is noted to be a high-risk medication requiring monitoring. Bruising is attributed to prednisone and should resolve with discontinuation. Patient to schedule blood work at front desk. Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
